newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar gains ahead of G7 summit, stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar gains ahead of G7 summit, stocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar retained its gains on the yen after President Bill Clinton helped reassure markets that a summit of leading industrial nations starting on Friday would not become a forum for a U.S.-Japan trade row.

European bourses were mixed despite a good start on Wall Street. Frankfurt closed at a record high, helped by the dollar, but London was well into the red in the early afternoon after voltaile trading.

The U.S. currency climbed half a yen as world leaders gathered for the three-day meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) in Denver. Remarks by Clinton helped to kill market talk that Washington would criticise Tokyo at the talks because of the recent jump in its trade surplus.

Exchange rates are a touchy issue in Japanese-American relations because a strong dollar helps Tokyo's exports to the United States but the benign outcome of a meeting between Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto soothed market anxieties.
Traders closely watched the meeting on Thursday for signs of heightened trade tensions but there were none.

Clinton voiced concern about Japan's rising merchandise trade surplus, which rose more than 200 percent in May, but added that foreign exchange rates should not be used as tools to manipulate trade imbalances, U.S. officials said.
Currency dealers saw this as a signal that the Clinton administration would not resort to calls for a weaker dollar to help to redress the trade imbalance, as it has done in the past.

"I expect the G7 to make a very neutral foreign exchange statement and it will probably have limited impact on trade," said Mike Malpede, senior foreign exchange analyst at Refco Group Ltd in New York.
"But it probably opens the dollar up for a little bit of dollar buying against the yen," he added.

The dollar was quoted at 114.62 yen, compared with 114.09 in late trade on Thursday. Concern that Denver would become the setting for a row had driven the dollar down as low as 112.75 earlier this week.

A long rally by the dollar reached a four-and-a-half year high of 127.46 yen on May 1. But traders largely ignored the two G7 summits earlier this year calling for an end to its climb and for more currency stability.

The dollar also climbed half a pfennig against the mark, which had a bad day against other European currencies. Sterling climbed to a 58-month high of 2.86 marks by mid-afternoon on prospects of higher British interest rates.

The stronger dollar helped boost some European bourses. Frankfurt floor ended at a new peak, up 39 points to 3,788.27 on 30-share DAX index, although gains on the after-hours IBIS index were modest after earlier touching a trading high at 3801.35 points.
"The market is still in very good shape," said one trader. Dealings in the afternoon will focus on Wall Street, which has been the driving factor for the German share market.
"The market right now is more focussed on the U.S. right now instead of on domestic factors," said another trader.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, flitted in and out of profit in volatile morning trade before sliding by one percent on the FTSE 100 index in the afternoon with nothing to sustain any upward momentum.
"There's no guts in the market and nothing to go for," said one dealer.

The bourse, which has fallen 140 points in the past week, has been dogged by worries of higher interest rates and fears the new Labour government's first budget on July 2 will contain bad news for investors.
The market has been unsettled by persistent press reports that finance minister Gordon Brown will scrap a tax break on dividend payments to major corporate investors.
In Paris, stocks made useful gains but trade was thin with investors digesting the implications of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's first major policy address on Thursday.

"There's not a lot of interest or a lot of volume," a broker said. "Although we were expecting some clarifications, a lot of doubt remains. A lot of decisions have been put off to September so uncertainty persists."
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7316 marks and 114.65 yen, compared with 1.7247 and 114.09 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 49.7 points at 4,604.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 17.41 points at 2,757.10.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 39.00 at 3788.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $338.20, a four-month low, against $339.75 on Thursday. Silver was barely changed at $4.76.
